channel.title: Research Tape
channel.description: A daily AI-in-finance research tape: arXiv and SSRN, six items or fewer.

item.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Financial Question Answering: Evidence from the FinQA Benchmark
item.description: Retrieval augmentation lifted a 4-billion-parameter financial QA model from 17.2% to 64.4% exact match, matching parameter-efficient fine-tuning at 63.9%.

item.title: Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core
item.description: A protected invariant core cut a 24.6% sector drawdown to 0.3% and lowered maximum drawdown under all 50 random entry policies.

item.title: When News Gets Old: Portfolio Allocation with Reinforcement Learning and Large Language Models
item.description: Filtering old news yielded 18.43% annual net returns for LLM portfolios with four-week delays, beating all news-using RL strategies.

item.title: Intraday Forecasting Ability and Liquidity Provision of Institutional Traders
item.description: One passive execution raised intraday P&L by 1.28 currency units versus none, exceeding the 1.19-unit gain from a one-standard-deviation forecasting increase.

item.title: Headline Emphasis and Stock Returns: Evidence from Counterfactual Headlines
item.description: A one-standard-deviation rise in headline divergence predicts nine basis points higher next-month returns through initial overreaction and later correction.

item.title: The Common Advice: Evidence on AI Redundancy in Stock Prices
item.description: After ChatGPT, common AI signals still forecast positive earnings announcement returns, indicating market underreaction rather than AI-driven overreaction.

item.title: CrashGym: Measuring the Decision Value of Experimentation for LLM Agents in Counterfactual Market Crashes
item.description: Laboratory access cuts Luna's mean market-crash decision regret by 57.4 percent versus observe-only deployment.

item.title: VQuant: An Agentic Large Language Model Architecture for Automated Quantitative Financial Analysis and Document Generation: Reasoning-Augmented Tool Orchestration, In-Loop Numerical Computation, and Multi-Format Reporting
item.description: VQuant reports no empirical measurements of accuracy hallucination latency or cost for its agentic finance platform.

item.title: Sealed Before the Open: A Verifiable Standard for Measuring AI Forecasts of Financial Markets
item.description: Eleven large language models sealed market forecasts into a Bitcoin-anchored hash chain before the New York open.

item.title: Understanding the Inner Workings of a State-Space Foundation Model for Limit Order Books
item.description: An 8.2-million-parameter Mamba model decodes LOB order-flow imbalance at R²≈0.59 on unseen equities.

item.title: What Prediction-Market Contracts Reveal at Launch: Trading Volume and Dispute Risk
item.description: Prediction-market launch features predict log-volume at out-of-sample R squared 0.747 but fail temporal generalization to later listing formats.

item.title: LOB-Impact Benchmark: Emergent Market Impact in Generative Limit Order Book Models
item.description: Autoregressive LOB generators trained only on next-token prediction show emergent market impact with exponents 0.63 to 1.21, though none decays during relaxation.

item.title: Testing semi-strong market efficiency in Brazilian football: A risk-adjusted machine learning approach
item.description: Seven machine learning forecasters lose to Brazilian football's closing line on log loss, and half-Kelly staking destroys most capital at zero edge.

item.title: Candlestick Words Improve Intraday Volatility Forecasts Beyond HAR and GARCH
item.description: Candlestick-word features improve 15-minute volatility forecasts beyond HAR and GARCH after volatility spikes, but add nothing at daily frequency.

item.title: From SEC Filings to Financial Signals: Evaluating LLMs on Stock Market Reactions and Analyst Forecasts
item.description: Adding cross-sectional fundamental ranks to 10-Q MD&A text raises LLM return-ranking RankIC by about 0.009, while analyst-summary context adds no comparable gain.

item.title: Unbounded Losses, Unchecked Inputs: Measuring the Safeguards of LLM Options-Trading Agents
item.description: Options-trading agents need loss limits enforced at the order boundary, since 13 of 26 surveyed systems can reach unbounded loss.

item.title: More Mentions, Less Information? Diagnosing Identity and Alignment in Reddit Embeddings for Volatility Forecasting
item.description: Most of WSB embeddings' standalone volatility fit reflects firm identity, and their gain over HAR is largely eliminated by alignment shuffling.

item.title: Reliable Before Profitable: QuantHarness for Governing Financial Strategy Development with LLM Agents
item.description: QuantHarness reaches 90.72% task success on FinRelBench versus 74.23–84.54% for comparison systems, under the evaluated protocol.

item.title: Beyond Behavioral Accuracy: Evaluating Individual-Level Fidelity in LLM Investor Simulation
item.description: No evaluated LLM reliably beats a recent-activity persistence baseline for trade occurrence, and buy-sell structure stays hard to reproduce.

item.title: Combinatorial Arbitrage in Prediction Markets
item.description: Logical arbitrage across Polymarket contracts survived spreads and fees, yielding 2.2% guaranteed profit on settled portfolios in full-depth order-book replays.

item.title: Faithful by Construction? An Exact Test of LLM Explanations for Constrained Portfolio Optimization Decisions
item.description: LLM explanations of linear-program portfolio decisions name zero-effect limits as drivers in 77-89% of cases, so they need solver-certificate checks.

item.title: Which Outcome Should Teach an LLM Reader? A Verified FOMC Benchmark and Reward-Design Evidence for Outcome-Guided Agents in Finance
item.description: Pre-meeting equity returns are learnable from FOMC minutes at out-of-sample R² 0.50, while the next policy-rate change shows no detectable text signal.

item.title: Where Backtests and Live Trading Part Ways: Six Defects from One Intraday System
item.description: In one intraday US equity system, every backtest-live drift traced to two paths that should agree but had drifted apart.

item.title: What does a Rejection Mean? A Retrospective Audit of a Registered Trading-rule Archive
item.description: Of 23 nominal exclusions among 210 rejected rules, 22 survive a training-series re-verification, yet all carry secondary stopping failures.

item.title: When Judges Agree and Are Wrong: Consistency-Accuracy Dissociation as a Blind Spot for Label-Free Evaluation
item.description: On four financial QA datasets, 60% of wrong answers sit in high-consistency regions, so agreement-based label-free evaluation misses confident errors.

item.title: How Much Screening Buys a Second? Speed, Selection, and the Maker's Spread
item.description: A twelve-second maker must screen at least 84.5% of informed flow to match a one-second venue, versus 71.1% under a Gaussian model.

item.title: When Does "Post-Call" Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks
item.description: Moving from call-start to completion proxy flips return signs for 9.4% of 552 earnings calls, so labels depend on the declared outcome clock.

item.title: Trading Costs and Machine-Learning Return Forecasts
item.description: In U.S. stocks at $500 million, trading costs matter in portfolio construction, not the loss: spread-gated liquidity weighting lifts net Sharpe from -0.38 to 0.42.

item.title: Reading the News Without Hindsight: NoLBERT Topics and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
item.description: Benchmarking news attention shocks against 63 trading days instead of 5 raises out-of-sample rank IC for every news reader tested.

item.title: The Marginal Yield of LLM-Guided Alpha Search: Search Effort, Information and Investment Value
item.description: In this setup, additional LLM factor proposals improve training scores but add no net return distinguishable from zero.

item.title: Expressed distress and portfolio risk in LLM investment advice
item.description: In this preregistered test, client distress cut LLM allocations above a tolerance-matched volatility reference from 12.2% to 2.8%.

item.title: No Name, No Gain? Unpacking Entity Bias in LLM Financial
item.description: In WSJ headlines, retaining firm names raises LLM sentiment's return predictability across all six models tested, a gain read as leakage.

item.title: Where Does Liquidity Go Around EIA Releases? Order-Level Evidence From CME Energy Futures, With Implications For Backtest Queue Models
item.description: Near-mid depth in CME crude and gas futures stays depleted after EIA releases, but release days cannot be separated from a Wednesday-Thursday 10:30 effect.

item.title: Does Statistical Arbitrage Survive in Indian Equity Derivatives? Evidence from Distance Pairs, Factor Residuals, and Machine Learning (2010- 2025)
item.description: Daily statistical arbitrage on NSE turns negative after statutory taxes and fees, since break-even needs costs at 0.38x institutional levels that statute prevents.

item.title: Equal-information evaluation of credit assignment in modular financial reinforcement learning
item.description: Residual-based credit allocation is exactly reproduced by a loss-budget control under the disclosed interface, so attribution adds no decision-relevant information.

item.title: When does Model Capacity Help? A Natural Experiment in Signal-to-Noise using US and Indian Equity Markets
item.description: In India's thin, low-SNR market, added model capacity does not improve on a linear predictor that has a significant out-of-sample IC.

item.title: How Well Do LLMs Perform in Peer Review? Evidence from Finance and Accounting
item.description: An LLM's judgements of correctness predict top-three finance publication, but its judgements of significance carry no such information.

item.title: Mind the Gap: LLM Extraction of Climate Scenario Financial-Impact Disclosures and Their Pricing in Hong Kong Equity and Credit Markets
item.description: Hong Kong equity returns and bond spreads show no visible response to climate-disclosure levels, at a minimum detectable three-day abnormal return of about 1.6%.

item.title: Model-Informed Gold Revisions Inflate Measured Accuracy: A Versioned Gold-Standard Protocol for LLM Extraction of ESG Data
item.description: Model-prompted revisions to ESG gold labels raised measured accuracy 5.1 points with predictions unchanged, so benchmarks should version references.

item.title: Market Impact Estimation via Causal Foundation Models
item.description: On a synthetic confounded prior, a causal foundation model tracks the unbiased impact oracle, but transfer requires encoding metaorders as added flow.

item.title: A Systematic Benchmark of Vector Stock Embeddings
item.description: Stock embeddings decisively beat a leak-free raw-correlation baseline but tie or trail raw return series on sub-industry retrieval in idealised, full-survivor panels.

item.title: MemTrial: Learning When to Trust Memory in LLM Portfolio Agents
item.description: Counterfactual credit for memories, not raw outcomes, keeps LLM portfolio agents within 2.2% of equal-weight on two benchmarks when experience values fail to generalize.

item.title: Beyond Isolation: LLM-Guided Hypergraph Learning across Documents and Horizons for Volatility Prediction from Conference Calls
item.description: Linking earnings calls across firms through shared LLM-built business-condition factors improves volatility forecasts over 5- to 60-day horizons versus transcript, graph, and financial baselines.

item.title: Consistent But Lenient: Large Language Models Versus Human Underwriters on Borderline Consumer Credit Decisions
item.description: On borderline credit files, LLM reviewers are more consistent than humans yet approve 79% versus 46%, so consistency alone cannot justify deployment.

item.title: Do LLM Valuation Agents Read the Filing? Metamorphic Tests of Filing Fidelity on Korean Listed Firms
item.description: Even with arithmetic delegated to Python, none of four preregistered primary hypotheses survives Holm correction across 150 Korean firms.

item.title: Look-ahead index membership and the relative accuracy of stock forecast
item.description: Look-ahead index rosters bias forecast comparisons against ML models, shrinking the Nasdaq-100 ML advantage over small size by about 90%.

item.title: OOM-RL II: Reality Is an Oracle, Not a Debugger Provenance-Constrained Diagnosis in Continually Evolving Agent-Engineered Systems
item.description: External outcome feedback can constrain claims about a trading system's returns but cannot identify which evolving procedure produced them without provenance binding.

item.title: Agents Propose, Code Decides: An Autonomous Research Loop Framework to Build an Equity Alpha Model
item.description: Agent-proposed predictors held their rank IC out of sample, but the hedged long-short retained only about half its expected Sharpe.

item.title: Agent Policy-Value Audit: Separating Transition Composition from Event Selection in Financial LLM Agents
item.description: The agent's +15.2 bps/event gross deployment value is explained by transition composition, leaving selection value at -10.6 bps and no detectable skill.

item.title: Noisy Financial Machine Learning
item.description: Against the panel historical mean rather than the zero forecast, only flexible nonlinear models show consistent gains, concentrated in small, value and illiquid stocks.

item.title: Large Language Models and Information Frictions in Corporate Bonds
item.description: LLM-read earnings calls forecast rating migration a year ahead, and bond returns only where analysts disagreed, while post-earnings drift is not explained by it.

item.title: MintEval: Do LLMs Implement the Trading Strategy You Asked For? A Behavioural-Equivalence Benchmark for Natural-Language-to-Strategy Code
item.description: A frontier model silently diverges from the requested strategy on 27.5% of tasks, and a recent LLM-judge benchmark accepts every such failure.

item.title: Mixture-of-Experts for Cryptocurrency Order Execution: Training Stability, Tail Risk, and Failure Modes
item.description: Annealed exploration alone eliminates policy collapse in this environment, making expert partitioning unnecessary, and within-policy tail risk rises monotonically with K.

item.title: Silent Implementation Shortfall in LLM-Written Trading Code
item.description: Frontier LLMs silently diverge from trading strategy intent on over a quarter of tasks.

item.title: Artifact Integrity Does Not Imply Temporal Integrity: Evaluating Evidence-Bound Gates for Financial Research Agents
item.description: Financial artifacts with verified byte integrity can still contain temporally invalid information.

item.title: LLM Pricing Agents as Rote Learners
item.description: Increased prompt context makes LLM pricing agents more consistent without making them more accurate.

item.title: Common AI Information and Capital Allocation
item.description: AI progress expands investor information but reduces price informativeness for firms, worsening capital allocation.

item.title: Calibrated Gating in Financial RAG: Small External Controllers versus LLM Self-Assessment across Model Scales
item.description: A 0.3B calibrated model beats LLM self-assessment for financial RAG evidence-sufficiency gating.

item.title: LLM-Driven Sentiment Shocks and Nonlinear Contagion in Global Banking Networks: A Hybrid SEM–ANN–GARCH Approach
item.description: LLM sentiment shocks correlate positively with financial contagion in banking networks.

item.title: Do Your Own Research: Learning to Forecast by Learning to Search
item.description: Outcome-based training teaches agents evidence discipline, reducing searches while improving forecast calibration.

item.title: Large Language Models, Debt Renegotiation, and Contract Enforcement
item.description: LLM-written messages outperform human-written messages in distressed-debt renegotiation.

item.title: LiveOption: Evaluating LLM Agents in Structured Option Trading with Nonlinear Payoffs
item.description: LLM agents underperform on structured option trading with nonlinear payoffs.

item.title: EverMine: Dissecting the Self-Evolution of Research Capabilities in Long-Horizon Alpha Research
item.description: Capability evolution provides no consistent gains in alpha discovery.

item.title: RICE-Alpha: Reliability-Informed Correction with Event Graphs for LLM-Agent Stock Forecasting
item.description: Historical event continuation adds forecast value when temporally grounded and reliability-calibrated.

item.title: From Search to Research: Exploring Search Scaling in Autonomous Quantitative Factor Mining
item.description: Model capability matters more than search depth in initial autonomous research.

item.title: An Integrated Framework of Financial Feature States, Scenario Candidates and a Lightweight Local Selection Model: A Matched-Information Comparison for S&P 500 Price-Path Selection
item.description: Lightweight language models underperform conventional baselines for S&P 500 price-path selection despite financial adaptation.

item.title: Do Narratives Lead Prices, Or Follow Them? Sentiment, Price Positioning, And Measurement Disagreement In Bitcoin
item.description: Bitcoin prices predict sentiment, reversing the leading-indicator interpretation of published sentiment indices.

item.title: Epistemic Calibration and Latency Advantages of System One Probabilistic Agents in Limit Order Book Microstructure: An Empirical and Multi-Agent Evaluation
item.description: Autoregressive LLMs encounter prohibitive latencies (3.5–12 seconds) when deployed in electronic financial markets.

item.title: Silicon Cartels: Detector Orientation in Multi-Agent Pricing Testbeds
item.description: Testbed detector calibration against low-variance controls reverses polarity in higher-variance deployment environments.

item.title: Agentic Regulatory Intelligence: A Human-Supervised Multi-Agent System Architecture for Financial Crime Pattern Monitoring and Regulatory Guidance Generation
item.description: Regulatory guidance for financial crimes lags 12–57 months after typology emergence, extending criminal opportunities.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence, Model Monoculture, and Bank Credit Allocation
item.description: AI development increases convergence in bank credit allocation, reducing system-wide lending diversity.

item.title: What the Fed Hears and What It Concludes: Supply-Chain Narratives and U.S. Inflation Forecasting ⋆
item.description: FOMC narratives improve inflation forecast accuracy while Beige Book narratives do not.

item.title: Order Invariance at the Last Language-Model Boundary: A Pre-Registered Test of an LLM Evidence Synthesizer Inside a Deterministic Trading Architecture
item.description: Language model nondeterminism, not input order sensitivity, drives trading system uncertainty.

item.title: When Stress Tests Miss the Risk: Statistical Scenario Analysis for Financial Portfolios
item.description: Standard scenario analysis substantially understates portfolio risk by overlooking factor dependence.

item.title: Adaptive State Representation and Critical Explainability Evaluation for A2C-Based Algorithmic Carbon Allowance Trading
item.description: A2C trading agent performance is sensitive to random initialization despite high reported Sharpe ratios.

item.title: Abstention Is Not Neutral: Ablating the LLM in an LLM Trading Agent
item.description: Language model trading agent abstention is primarily determined by prompt wording, not market conditions.

item.title: Residual Learning in Empirical Asset Pricing
item.description: Deep neural networks outperform shallow models in asset pricing when trained with residual learning.

item.title: Propose, Don't Judge: An Anytime-Valid Referee for LLM Agents That Mine Investment Factors
item.description: Frozen referees outperform leaky referees at controlling spurious factors.

item.title: The Price of Thought: Does Test-Time Reasoning Pay in LLM Trading?
item.description: LLM test-time reasoning changes trading decisions without reliably improving returns.

item.title: What Analysts Miss: Predicting Consensus Forecast Errors from Earnings Calls
item.description: Analyst forecast errors are predictable from earnings-call language and profitable to trade around announcements.

item.title: The Externality of Learning: Adaptive AI and Market Resilience
item.description: Shared learning histories improve market resilience when policies are learned via locality-sensitive algorithms.

item.title: An Auditable Public-Data U.S. Equity Research Pipeline: Point-in-Time Factors, Asset Pricing, Portfolio Construction, and Walk-Forward Machine Learning
item.description: Higher R-squared in multifactor models doesn't translate to stable after-cost portfolio outperformance.

item.title: DefaultGNN: A Dual-Perspective GNN Framework for Predicting Corporate Default from Buyer-Seller Transaction Networks
item.description: Buyer-seller transaction networks predict default better than financial data for information-sparse firms.

item.title: When the Market Moves but the Model Does Not: Stale Financial Information in LLMs
item.description: LLMs generate persistent trading losses when forecasting beyond their training data without current price information.

item.title: The Anonymity Paradox: Identity Disclosure, Online Information Production, and Stock Price Efficiency
item.description: Real-name policies reduce stock price informativeness by suppressing retail information production on social platforms.

item.title: Planning External-Data Adoption in Energy-Market Forecasting: A Matched Decision Framework for Global News
item.description: Best energy forecasts use market data alone, not augmented with external news.

item.title: Forecasting, Forward Contracting, and Retailer Performance in a Regulated Electricity Market
item.description: Better spot-price forecasts only improve electricity trading profits if retailers can flexibly adjust forward positions.

item.title: Systematic Alpha Discovery in Foreign Exchange Markets A Two-phase Research Program: From Exhaustive Structural-factor Search to Fundamentals-Driven Machine Learning
item.description: Exhaustive FX factor searches identify zero exploitable edges under statistical validation.

item.title: Asymmetric Volatility Transmission Between AI Compute Infrastructure and Regional Power Grids: Evidence from Quantile Connectedness Under Extreme Market States
item.description: Volatility transmission between AI infrastructure and power grids reverses during crises.

item.title: Label alchemy: Target engineering for improved stock selection
item.description: Label choice drives larger stock-selection performance variation than model or feature selection.

item.title: Prices or implied volatilities? Choosing the loss function in machine learning option pricing
item.description: Training option-pricing models on price errors beats implied-volatility loss by 25%.

item.title: Agentic AI as a Lens on Human Decision Making: Field Experimental Evidence from Dynamic Pricing
item.description: AI pricing advantage exploits incumbent conventions, suggesting performance gains are transient.

item.title: Inflation narratives and risk premia
item.description: Demand-minus-supply narratives predict inflation risk premia better than PMI or forecasters.

item.title: LLM-Based Semantic Surprises in FOMC Communication: Asset Prices and Financial-Market Stress
item.description: Fed semantic novelty increases financial stress only in high-stress market regimes.

item.title: Welcome to the Factor Zoo: Where Mutual Fund Alpha Hides
item.description: LASSO benchmarks reveal active mutual fund alpha Fama-French models obscure.
